exposure: delayed cord clamping (DCC) of at least 60 s
cohort: 620 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants born to 545 mothers
finding: Delayed cord clamping of at least 60 seconds did not increase maternal bleeding complications during cesarean delivery in VLBW infants.
mod_finding: Delayed cord clamping of at least 60 seconds did not increase maternal bleeding complications during cesarean delivery of very low birth weight infants.
